messages.body_plain:
Yes the border is actually there, and that is due to the gray shading
of the chunk output. Two approaches to eliminate it:

1. chunk option background='white'
2. use this slightly modified hook instead of hook_rgl:

knit_hooks$set(rgl = function(before, options, envir) {
  if (before) return()
  # escape the plot from the kframe environment
  paste('\\end{kframe}', hook_rgl(before, options, envir),
'\n\\begin{kframe}', sep = '')
})

If you want to clip the image, you can install ImageMagick and set
another chunk hook, say, knit_hooks$set(crop = hook_pdfcrop), and
<<rgl=TRUE, crop=TRUE>>=. This was explained in p6-7 in the graphics
manual: https://github.com/downloads/yihui/knitr/knitr-graphics.pdf

messages.subject: wrapping knit messages/warning for logging
messages.body_plain:
What I want to do is wrap all the output that knit generates (progress output reported on standard out/R Console) so that I can utilize the logging package (http://logging.r-forge.r-project.org); this way, when I rerun multiple scheduled reports on a daily basis, I can get timestamp on each message for ease for greping/etc/etc.

So I tried using a knitr output hook to redirect the messages/warnings to a log file (as a simple example)  (from an earlier discussion on this group), i.e.:

<<setup, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE>>=
  hook_log = function(x, options)
  {
      cat(x, file='messages.txt', append=TRUE)
  }
  knit_hooks$set(warning = hook_log, message = hook_log)
@

This however only redirects any messages that I have in my own chunks in the .Rnw file i.e.

<<setup-code, echo=FALSE>>
message("Hello World")
@

but the rest of the progress output is not redirected.

Is there any way to force all the messages that knit() generates to use my hook_log as well?

I also tried wrapping my call to knit using withCallingHandlers function in base R i.e:

suppressMessages(withCallingHandlers(knit2pdf(input='foo.Rnw', envir=new.env()), simpleMessage = function(w){loginfo(w, logger='tca')}))

This worked partially - it only wrapped the first line and last line i.e.:

2012-11-08 17:18:28.588 INFO:logger:simpleMessage in message(ifelse(progress, "\n\n", ""), "processing file: ", input):

processing file: ../src/foo.Rnw
  |>>                                                               |   2%
  ordinary text without R code

....

2012-11-08 17:18:59.709 INFO:logger:simpleMessage in message("output file: ", normalizePath(output), ifelse(progress, : output file: F:\foo.tex

loginfo is a function in the logging package mentioned above.

The above example works when using a simple arbitrary function i.e:

R> library(logging)
R> fooFunc <- function() { message(paste('Hello World: ', Sys.time())) }
R> addHandler(writeToConsole, logger="mylogger", level="FINEST")
R> suppressMessages(withCallingHandlers(fooFunc(), simpleMessage = function(w){logwarn(w, logger='mylogger')}))
2012-11-08 17:23:49.219 WARNING:mylogger:simpleMessage in message(paste("Hello World: ", Sys.time())): Hello World:  2012-11-08 17:23:49.156

R> fooFunc()
Hello World:  2012-11-08 17:24:08.529

If anyone has other suggestions, please let me know

Thanks

-Haider

Great question, and you can do it with the development version of
knitr on Github.

library(devtools); install_github('knitr', 'yihui')

insert it into a document; in your case, you only need

@

Now you showed how you really called knit(), and that revealed the
problem: you are not supposed to specify the output file to another
directory.

Here is my first principle of working with R: set the working
directory before you working on anything; from then on, always use
relative paths instead of absolute paths.

setwd('~/Latex/')
library(knitr)
knit('aknit1.Rnw')
# or knit('aknit1.Rnw', output = 'aknit1.tex')

But I think you really need a better editor such as RStudio or
Emacs/ESS, which will take care of this automatically. It wastes time
to type setwd(), library(knitr) and knit() every time.

The reason for the failure in your case is, you wrote aknit1.tex to a
place which is not your working directory, but your figures were
written to the figure/ directory relative to the current working
directory (i.e. /home/john/figure/figure/unnamed-chunk-1.pdf), so the
tex file does not really know where are the figures.

Regards,
Yihui

\input{my-header}

Package xcolor Error: Undefined color model `'.

\documentclass[svgnames,12pt]{article}\usepackage{graphicx, color}

I saw a similar issue from last year, (https://github.com/yihui/knitr/issues/91) but it had to do with tikz images being created within knitr.
